newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Trial of Mujib's killers to begin in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Trial of Mujib's killers to begin in Bangladesh.

text.p: Bangladeshi police have laid charges against 25 people, mostly ex-army officers, over the killing of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in a 1975 coup, and their trial is expected to begin on Monday.
The documents used to frame the charges have been submitted to the court of Dhaka's Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, where the accused will be produced on January 20, police said on Friday.
The long-awaited trial is set to begin nearly seven months after Mujib's daughter Sheikh Hasina took over as Bangladesh's Prime Minister following general elections in June.

Hasina and her only sister, Sheikh Rehana, survived the August 15, 1975, coup because they were abroad at the time. In all, 32 people, including Mujib, his wife and three sons were killed in what was the country's first army revolt.
Police have already arrested 10 of the accused, including three former army officers and Mujib's information minister.

Six other army officers, suspected masterminds of the coup, were assigned to diplomatic jobs abroad by Mujib's successors -- ex-presidents Khandaker Mushtaque Ahmed and General Ziaur Rahman, husband of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Lieutenant-General Zia was killed in an abortive mutiny in 1981 and Ahmed died of illness last year.
All six have absconded. Hasina's government has urged all countries not to grant them political asylum or shelter but has yet to bring any of them home.
Ahmed, made president following Mujib's assassination, issued an ordinance protecting the coup leaders from legal prosecution and his successor Zia did not change it.
It was repealed by parliament in November.
Police declined to give details of the charges or name all the accused until the court sits.
Newspapers said on Friday that the two late presidents have also been named as co-conspirators in the assassination, a move the New Nation said would inflame the political situation.
"The inclusion of the name of late president Zuar Rahman in the charge-sheet of Mujib murder case is going to create yet another undesirable situation in the country," the daily said.
Hasina said after taking over that "everything (regarding the trial) will be done within the purview of law, but the killers will no longer enjoy the luxury of freedom."
